notes:
Big-version application release: per-page deep audit plus tiered automation (docs/263 P0–P6), together with the completion of the P4 finding→action entry (docs/279). Adds: diagnosable generator refusal reasons with a stable refusalCode (P0); navigation-tree extraction and the selection UI (P1); PageAudit v2 with per-page score, field-level GEO, static UX observations, cross-page rollups, the deep-audit store/route/task kind and the deep-audit page (P2); the official wp/v2 independent normalised readback as a second measuring channel, plus the direction-B verification semantics that let content_edit and internal_link_add reach verified without loosening byte comparison (P3); the finding→action recipe catalogue, zero-typing request creation from one finding, cross-page batch creation and the origin enumeration extension (P4); risk tiers, per-site automation policy, in-place candidate editing, tier-4 human patch artefacts and the review inbox (P5); standing authorizations with a daily quota, the automation admin page and the delivery-gate fix (P6).

This release additionally connects the per-page entry in the UI (report page and deep-audit page) and lets a finding source be resolved from the deep-audit store as well as the report store — without that, every entry on the deep-audit page returned 404, because deep-audit page results and rollups live only in deepAuditStore while the route read only reportStore. Anti-forgery is unchanged: a finding must still genuinely hit in this organisation's and this site's stored audit results.

This application release does not itself upgrade production, and it does not satisfy the P4 production acceptance run (a real production site, N pages missing Meta Description, one batch seo_update through generate → approve → two confirmations → runner execution). It does not cover the site-wide 37-check (check:) axis either: those findings are site-aggregate with no per-page hit to prove, so no entry is fabricated for them; giving them one needs a product answer for which page a site-level finding applies to. The separate WordPress official-integration work is NOT part of this tag — it remains uncommitted in the working tree. The 199-item agent matrix remains 197 accepted / 2 open (216-A5-01/02), gated on the 2026-10-27 dual-window observation.

Database: additive migrations 048–050 on top of 047. 048 only widens the agent_requests origin enumeration to include 'page_finding', and is the single statement in this release that takes a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on agent_requests (DROP/ADD of the same CHECK, executed inside the migrator's per-migration transaction); 049 and 050 create new tables with FORCE RLS and organisation-isolation policies. Verified on a database that had genuinely been at 047: all three applied, agent_requests_origin_check now contains 'page_finding', and both new tables report relrowsecurity = relforcerowsecurity = true with an organization_id = current_setting('app.organization_id') policy.

No production-backup rehearsal was run for this release, and none is claimed. CI applies the published image's migrator twice against a fresh PostgreSQL 16 to prove clean application and idempotency; that does not exercise an upgrade from a production-shaped 047 database with real data volume. Never downgrade or restore an old whole database during application rollback.

Rollback target: v0.2.23 application images only. The three migrations are additive or schema-compatible, so v0.2.23 code runs on the new schema; agent automation, standing authorizations and the deep-audit UI become unavailable in the old version and their rows must remain in place for re-upgrade. Before rolling back, stop outbound execution claims, inspect and preserve every in-flight or unknown operation, and retain authorizations, receipts and evidence; never replay unknown writes. This does not roll back any website content change — that requires its own approved restoration request.

Bootstrap: unchanged from v0.2.23 — this release introduces no new control-plane protocol, so an installation already on v0.2.23 upgrades with the updater it has. Explicit rollback requires the exact rollbackCompatibleFrom array member.

Validation: full API suite 2140 passed / 181 skipped (including the new finding-source resolver, request-planner and cross-page batch cases, and the web-contract envelope check); both packages typecheck with zero errors; pnpm --filter web build succeeds and lists /report/[id]/deep in the route table; verify-history opens 173/173 historical records; the P4 entry browser verification passes 41/41 against real components and real Chrome with cross-page rollups computed by the real engine (evidence docs/evidence/263-p4-entry-2026-10-15). CI must build and publish the final source images; their digests, provenance and any production acceptance are recorded only after deployment.
